extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners involved in U.S. patent prosecution
extracted.subtask_short: IDS preparation for U.S. patent prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, formatting, and filing Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) in U.S. patent applications (including continuing applications, national stage/PCT entries, RCEs, and CPAs) to ensure consideration by examiners and compliance with 37 CFR 1.97–1.99 and related MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of prior art cited in parent application (continuing applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a continuing application that claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 to a parent application, information which has been considered by the Office in the parent application will be part of the file before the examiner and need not be resubmitted in the continuing application to have the information considered (but may be resubmitted if applicant desires the information to be printed on the patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part (37 CFR 1.53(b)) and CPAs (37 CFR 1.53(d)) as described. If resubmitting, the resubmitted list must comply with 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1) and timing rules of 37 CFR 1.97. Applicants are strongly discouraged from submitting PTO/SB/08 or PTO-892 forms from other applications because pre-filled examiner initials or application numbers may confuse the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS requirement when parent is an international application designating the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: When a continuing application claims benefit to an international application that designated the U.S., applicant must submit an IDS complying with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 listing documents cited in the international search report if applicant wishes to ensure that the information is considered by the examiner in the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1895 and § 609.03 for PCT national stage specifics. If relying on ISR citations for consideration or printing on the patent, follow the separate listing and copy requirements of 37 CFR 1.98 and related MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS list format requirements (37 CFR 1.98(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS listing must follow the format in 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1): (A) a specified format/identification for each page of an IDS, and U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications must be listed in a section separately from citations of other documents; (B) a column providing space next to each document for the examiner’s initials; and (C) a heading that identifies the list as an IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forms PTO/SB/08A and 08B to ensure compliance. Each page of the list must clearly identify the application number. Separate listing of U.S. patents/publications enables OCR capture of numbers for electronic retrieval and examiner use. Each page should bear a heading indicating it is an IDS to avoid mishandling or being treated as third‑party submissions (37 CFR 1.99).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements for items listed (37 CFR 1.98(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each item in an IDS must be properly identified: U.S. patents by inventor, patent number, and issue date; U.S. patent application publications by applicant (or inventor), publication number, and publication date; U.S. applications by inventor, eight-digit application number, and filing date; foreign patents/published foreign applications by country/office, document number, and publication date; publications by publisher, author, title, relevant pages, and date/place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For internet publications provide the URL and, where appropriate, an archive URL and retrieval date. If a cited U.S. application has been published or issued, list the publication or patent instead of the application. Pending U.S. applications may be listed under NPL or a separately labeled section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate-paper requirement for the IDS list
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of information complying with 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1) and identification requirements of 37 CFR 1.98(b) must be submitted in a separate paper and may not be incorporated into the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate list makes it easy for the examiner to indicate which documents have been considered and prevents misinterpretation of background citations as an IDS. Use PTO/SB/08A/08B where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legible copy requirements (37 CFR 1.98(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS must include a legible copy of: (A) each foreign patent; (B) each publication or the portion which caused it to be listed (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required by the Office); (C) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including the claims and drawings or the portion that caused it to be listed, unless the cited pending U.S. application is stored in the IFW system; and (D) all other information or the portion which caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications are not required unless requested by the Office. The IFW storage of a cited pending U.S. application waives the copy requirement for the specification/claims/drawings; however, if other material in the file is cited, copies of that material must be provided. Applicants may cite only a portion of a pending application if desired, and exceptions (cumulative/prior application reliance) may eliminate copy needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to copy requirement: prior-application reliance (37 CFR 1.98(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any patent, publication, pending U.S. application, or other information listed in an IDS is not required to be provided if: (A) the information was previously cited by or submitted to the Office in a prior application properly identified in the IDS and relied on for an earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120; and (B) the IDS submitted in the earlier application complies with 37 CFR 1.98(a)-(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both conditions are met, the examiner will consider the previously cited/submitted information in the prior application. This exception does not apply to information cited in an international application under the PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception to copy requirement for cumulative disclosures (37 CFR 1.98(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosures of two or more patents or publications listed in an IDS are substantively cumulative, the applicant may submit a copy of one such patent or publication without copies of the others if a statement is made that the others are cumulative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will consider only the submitted copy and will indicate that on the PTO/SB/08A/08B list. Beware: a reference that appears cumulative may nonetheless contain unique relevant teachings (see Semiconductor Energy Laboratory Co. v. Samsung Electronics Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise explanation of relevance for non-English information (37 CFR 1.98(a)(3)(ii) and MPEP III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each IDS must include a concise explanation of the relevance of listed information that is not in the English language, as presently understood by the individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) most knowledgeable about the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The concise explanation may be separate from the specification or part of it (if part, IDS must include pages/lines). If a complete English translation is submitted, no concise explanation is required. Translations need not be verified; machine translations are acceptable if they are actual translations. Submission of an English-language abstract or the English-language search report/action from a foreign office can satisfy the requirement. Do not submit partial translations or concise explanations that misdirect the examiner from key teachings (Semiconductor Energy Laboratory precedent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic and other media filing limitations for IDS content
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic means/medium for filing IDSs are not permitted except: (A) citations to U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, foreign patent documents, and NPLs in an IDS filed via the Office’s Electronic Filing System (EFS); or (B) a compact disc (CD) that has tables, sequence listings, or program listings included in a paper IDS in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CD cannot be used to submit an IDS listing or copies of the documents cited in the IDS. Published information (e.g., software visual output, video) may only be submitted if reduced to writing (screenshots, transcripts). See MPEP § 609.07 for EFS details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirements for IDS consideration (37 CFR 1.97) — four-stage framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedures under 37 CFR 1.97 link IDS submission to four stages: (1) for national apps: within three months of filing or before mailing of first Office action on the merits (later of); (1)(b)-(d) analogous for international/national stage/CPAs; (2) after period (1) but prior to prosecution close (before final OA, Notice of Allowance, or Ex parte Quayle); (3) after (2) but on or before issue-fee payment; (4) after (3) up to time the application can be effectively withdrawn from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDS filed within period (1) requires neither a fee nor a statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e). Filing date is date received in the Office, or earlier mailing date if accompanied by certificate of mailing/fax under 37 CFR 1.8 or compliant Priority Mail Express. If the last day of a 3‑month period falls on a Saturday, Sunday or federal holiday, IDS is timely if filed on the next succeeding business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of timely IDS on examiner actions (cannot make final first Office action)
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not be proper to make final a first Office action in a continuing application or in an application after the filing of an RCE if the information submitted in the IDS during the time period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(b) is used in a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an IDS is filed within the first-action/timely period and examiner uses the information to generate a new ground of rejection, the examiner should not make the first OA final; appropriate non-final practice must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national stage IDS handling and printing on patent (MPEP § 609.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: For PCT national stage applications, the examiner will consider U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, and U.S. pending applications cited in the ISR that are stored in USPTO IFW. The examiner will consider other documents from the ISR when the PCT/DO/EO/903 form indicates that both the search report and copies of the documents are present in the national stage file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no requirement that the examiner list the documents on a PTO-892; however, citations will not be printed on the face of the patent unless listed on a list that permits easy capture of the necessary information by the Office printing contractor. Use of form paragraphs (e.g., ¶6.53–6.55) or listing on PTO-892 are options. If copies required under 1.98 are not indicated on PCT/DO/EO/903, burden is on applicant to supply them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouragement of using other-applications' PST forms and page-identification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are strongly discouraged from submitting a list that includes copies of PTO/SB/08 or PTO-892 forms from other applications, because those forms may include examiner initials or application numbers of other files that will confuse the record. Each page of the list must clearly identify the application number of the application in which the IDS is being submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If list pages become separated, the Office must be able to associate pages with the proper application. Ensure every page has the correct application number and an IDS heading.
